title: Small atoms of knowledge, then composites
statement: Write what is to be known as small atoms of a few facts each, kept apart from the composite tasks that combine them.
example: One science workbook holds 1129 atoms and 385 composites across Grades K to 8, at 2.5 facts per atom.
detail: A science curriculum review workbook writes each grade as atoms, marks a review atom with where it was first taught and what is new, and adds multi-step composites that combine atoms; its summary gives 2.5 facts per atom in every grade (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Science/Science_Curriculum_Review_Workbook.xlsx`). A social studies standards workbook plans a four-step expansion per grade that includes breaking content into micro-atoms (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Texts/Misconception and alignment checks/Social studies/Consensus social science standards.xlsx`). It is a design; no outcome was measured. Each atom is marked new, or as a review naming where it was first taught, and the final integrated performance is defined by exemplars and a rubric rather than broken down further.
against: Both sources are drafts: all 189 reviewer-comment cells in one ledger are blank, which records no review rather than approval, and the course graph awaits academic review (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0150-science-g6-atom-composite-ledger.qmd`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/applied/g3-course-graph.qmd`).
